markdown_report:
SASRec with a gated recent-history residual and uniform multi-negative training remains the strongest first experiment at 0% progress. Its incremental benefit is unverified; separate architectural and objective effects before accepting the combination.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Users value recent mood/task matches and repeated narrow preferences. Recent pooling may strengthen current intent; retaining SASRec may preserve sustained preferences. (2) Unsupported upgrades and unnecessary replacements expose missing ownership and compatibility evidence. Neither recency nor interaction order resolves these unknowns. (3) Electronics has 14.95% wrong training-position rankings and a −0.4812 lower-decile margin. Similar embedding-similarity scores across categories do not establish collapse as the cause or predict validation improvement.

**Insights from related work.** (1) [eSASRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.06450) and [SCE](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.18721) motivate richer competition, while [gSASRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.07192) identifies objective calibration as a confound. (2) [HLSDMRec](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ipm.2025.104425) motivates immediate/enduring preference separation, but SASRec already aggregates history adaptively. The residual needs controls against simple averaging. (3) [Revisiting Graph Projections](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.09209) motivates directional associations, which cannot establish compatibility or satisfied needs.

The resulting framework has three directions:

| Direction | Existing mechanism | Proposed test | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Candidate discrimination | Sampled objectives | Uniform multi-negative softmax | Unobserved relevance |
| Intent resolution | Long/short preference fusion | Gated recent-history residual | Unknown current task |
| Follow-on utility | Directed interaction graphs | Smoothed transition residual | Unknown equipment ownership |

Three candidate ideas follow. Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each cell gives one positive and one limitation.

| Idea | Originality | Potential | User alignment | Model alignment | Difficulty |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Multi-negative softmax | 2: established; little novelty | 7: scalable; sampling-sensitive | 4: competition; no intent mechanism | 9: targets separation; training evidence only | 3: small loss; exclusions need care |
| **Gated recent residual + softmax** | 4: useful combination; familiar parts | 7: extensible; incremental benefit unknown | 8: recent/recurring intent; ownership unknown | 8: separation; gate may overfit | 4: small branch; serialization and controls |
| Directed transition residual | 5: asymmetric evidence; established graphs | 7: interpretable; sparse edges | 7: plausible tasks; compatibility uncertain | 6: ranking signal; popularity confounding | 5: sparse graph; prefix leakage risk |

Select the second idea. It explicitly targets broad associations displacing recent mood/task matches and isolated interactions displacing sustained narrow preferences. Multi-negative competition targets Electronics’ weak separation tail. These are hypotheses, not demonstrated remedies.

Train categories independently. Cross baseline/residual architectures with original BCE/64-negative candidate softmax. Use causal raw-embedding means over five positions, an identity-initialized projection, and a gate initialized near zero. Sample with replacement from category-local items excluding complete training histories; retain duplicate multiplicity. This supersedes duplicate masking. Specify safeguards and scoring exactly as below.

Prespecify checkpoints, equal-cost screening and promotion within 43,200 GPU-seconds. Select only by unchanged macro validation HR@10; report Electronics separately. Use paired category-stratified bootstrap intervals for fixed comparisons, disclose every inspected trial, and label adaptively selected gains exploratory. Preserve seeds, routing, splits, predictor serialization and diagnostic contracts.

idea.description: Add a small gated recent-history residual to SASRec and train candidate scores with uniform multi-negative candidate softmax. Use a four-cell architecture-by-objective ablation to establish whether either component contributes before accepting the combined model.
idea.motivation: The recent branch targets broad recommendations that displace current mood or task matches. Retaining SASRec provides a mechanism for sustained narrow preferences to remain influential when recent interactions are isolated. These explicitly address two diagnosed user-facing failures, although neither mechanism guarantees success. Multi-negative competition targets weak positive–negative separation, especially Electronics’ negative lower-decile margin. Equipment compatibility, ownership, satisfied needs and simulator traits remain unobserved; do not claim to solve or label them.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, four independent category routes, baseline splits, and int(os.environ.get('SASREC_EPOCHS', '200')). Write all artifacts beneath the trial directory. Preserve the actual RecHarness baseline's attention, padding, embedding scaling, tied output embeddings and normalization; document deviations from the official SASRec implementation rather than silently changing them.

At position t, compute m_t as the padding-masked mean of raw, unscaled item embeddings at max(0,t-4) through t, excluding position embeddings and all future items. Clamp the denominator to at least one and zero invalid outputs. Let h_t be the baseline's final normalized SASRec state. Set g_t = sigmoid(W[h_t;m_t]+b), with a vector gate W initialized to zero and b=-3. Set z_t = h_t + g_t * P(LN(m_t)), with P a bias-free d-by-d projection initialized to identity and LN having its usual unit scale and zero bias. Do not add another final normalization. This makes the initial residual small, not exactly zero. Use identical dropout settings across comparisons; use the same raw embedding lookup for pooling and tied candidate scoring.

For each user, define the category-local eligible set as all nonpadding item IDs minus the complete training-positive set. Construct this exclusion while user identity is available inside the dataset sampler; a truncated sequence cannot reconstruct it. Draw exactly 64 negatives independently with replacement for each valid position. Keep duplicate multiplicity; exclude no items using validation or test interactions. Explicitly skip and count users with zero eligible items in every experimental arm. Positives are training items and therefore already excluded. Do not also deduplicate or silently shrink K. These are unobserved items, not established dislikes; complete-training-history exclusion also uses later training interactions, so it is a deliberate training-sampling convention rather than an online prefix-only simulation.

Use uncorrected candidate cross-entropy L = logsumexp(s_positive, s_negative_1, ..., s_negative_64) - s_positive, averaged over valid positions. This is a 65-entry candidate objective, not an unbiased full-catalogue softmax approximation. Apply no LogQ or catalogue-size correction. Chunk positions when necessary while preserving the exact valid-position mean and gradients; do not alter K to resolve memory pressure. Preserve baseline optimizer and hyperparameters for the initial ablation. Fix and record sampler RNG streams separately from model initialization; share negative draws between the two architectures under each objective. The BCE control retains the baseline objective and negative count, so the objective comparison jointly changes loss and candidate count and must be described accordingly.

Maintain a training-only batch path carrying the sampled B-by-L-by-64 negatives while user identity remains internal to sampling. Provide a separate diagnostic loader yielding exactly (None, sequence, positive, negative), with all tensors B-by-L and one eligible sampled negative per valid position. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions; view.model must be the trained nn.Module. view.item_emb exposes its actual item embedding, log2feats returns fused states, and predict_score uses the identical tied-embedding scoring path. Preserve user_train, meta_data and review_data compatibility fields using only available data. Report category-based diagnostics as unavailable; do not infer unavailable item categories from the four dataset routes or invent reviews, ratings, prices or stores. Training margins are diagnostics, not selection metrics; logit scale changes can increase margins without improving ranking.

Save architecture version, window, gate/projection configuration, baseline hyperparameters, item mappings and state_dict beneath the trial directory. Update the predictor writer so working/predict.py reconstructs the exact trained module, calls eval(), disables gradients, applies identical sequence truncation/padding and routes every dataset correctly. Verify save/load score agreement on training-derived inputs. Continue full-catalogue unseen-item recommendations for five real training users per category through the existing simulator path; do not replace this with sampled-candidate recommendations.

Prespecify the four primary cells: baseline+BCE, residual+BCE, baseline+candidate-softmax, residual+candidate-softmax. Declare epoch checkpoints and deterministic promotion/tie rules before observing outcomes. Screen at equal measured GPU cost while retaining all categories, then promote within a reserved full-length budget; count baseline runs, failed trials, diagnostics and serialization checks toward 43,200 GPU-seconds. Optional later controls are last-item-only and recent-mean-only scorers, last-item residual, and fixed-coefficient recent residual; do not launch their full factorial automatically. They distinguish additional capacity, pooling, and learned gating, but remain untested unless budget permits.

Select exclusively using pinned four-category macro validation HR@10, with per-category results and Electronics reported separately. Where the existing host supplies per-user hit outcomes, compare fixed model pairs on identical users and candidates: bootstrap paired outcomes within each category for 10,000 CPU replicates using a declared seed, then report the macro difference, 95% percentile interval, category differences and discordant-hit counts. One additional hit changes macro HR@10 by 0.00125. If per-user outcomes are unavailable, omit intervals rather than modify the evaluator or manufacture them. Intervals condition on trained models and fixed candidates; they exclude training and negative-candidate randomness and do not correct adaptive validation selection. Disclose all inspected trials/checkpoints and describe selected gains as exploratory. No test access, external weights, new datasets or benchmark improvements are claimed.
idea.pseudocode:
prespecify four architecture/objective cells, checkpoints, GPU allocations and promotion rules
for each cell and each of the four existing dataset routes:
    reset baseline preprocessing/training seeds to 0/42
    initialize the unchanged SASRec backbone
    if residual enabled:
        initialize W=0, b=-3, P=identity, LN.scale=1, LN.bias=0
    build eligible item sets using complete training histories only
    for training batch from sampler that internally knows user IDs:
        sequence, positive, negatives = batch  # negatives B,L,K; K=1 or 64
        h = baseline_final_normalized_states(sequence)
        if residual enabled:
            raw = item_emb(sequence)  # no sqrt(d) scaling or positions
            m = causal_padding_masked_window_mean(raw, sequence != 0, window=5)
            g = sigmoid(linear(concat(h, m), W, b))
            z = h + g * P(LN(m))
        else:
            z = h
        if baseline BCE:
            loss = unchanged_baseline_BCE(z, positive, negatives[..., 0])
        else:
            # 64 eligible uniform draws WITH replacement; retain multiplicity
            scores = tied_embedding_dot(z, concat(positive[..., None], negatives))
            loss = mean_valid(logsumexp(scores, dim=-1) - scores[..., 0])
        update using baseline optimizer
        stop or checkpoint according to prespecified budget
    save state, architecture configuration and matching predictor writer output
    verify save/load scores on training-derived inputs
    run adapted diagnosis with a separate (None, seq, pos, neg) B-by-L loader
obtain pinned host validation outcomes at declared checkpoints
promote according to declared macro-HR@10 and GPU-budget rules
report all trials, category scores, fixed-pair uncertainty when available, and GPU cost
select by pinned macro validation HR@10; keep test labels unavailable

originality.positive: Combines an explicit causal recent-history residual with stronger candidate competition in a small, falsifiable adaptation of SASRec.
originality.negative: History pooling, gated preference fusion and multi-negative objectives are established; novelty lies mainly in the constrained combination and evaluation.

future_potential.positive: Component controls can reveal whether explicit recent intent contributes beyond adaptive attention and provide a foundation for temporal or directional extensions.
future_potential.negative: Incremental benefit is unverified, sparse histories may weaken gating, and missing ownership or compatibility evidence limits practical-utility claims.

code_difficulty.positive: The model adds only causal pooling, layer normalization, a small projection and a gate.
code_difficulty.negative: Complete-history sampling, separate diagnostic batches, exact predictor reconstruction, memory handling and controlled comparisons require careful integration.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Provides the causal self-attention baseline and tied item-scoring framework.
Its adaptive aggregation and connection to uniform aggregation motivate explicit pooling controls.
limitations: Does not establish the incremental value of this residual or infer equipment compatibility and satisfied needs.

related_work.title: Official SASRec implementation
contributions: Documents causal masking, padding handling, scaled input embeddings, unscaled tied output embeddings and final normalization.
limitations: The actual RecHarness baseline remains the implementation reference; substituting official-code details could introduce confounds.

related_work.title: eSASRec
contributions: Motivates sampled softmax alongside a strong sequential backbone.
limitations: Combined architectural and objective gains do not isolate the loss or establish gains on this benchmark.

related_work.title: SCE
contributions: Motivates allocating candidate-scoring computation to informative logits.
limitations: Its search-based approximation is more complex than the proposed initial uniform-sampling experiment.

related_work.title: gSASRec
contributions: Investigates negative-sampling overconfidence and generalized BCE.
Motivates treating objective calibration as a separate experimental factor.
limitations: Generalized BCE is distinct from candidate softmax, and its calibration assumptions do not transfer automatically to user-specific exclusions.

related_work.title: Turning Dross Into Gold Loss
contributions: Examines objective differences in sequential recommendation and motivates controlling loss when comparing architectures.
limitations: Does not establish the proposed recent-history residual's value.

related_work.title: HLSDMRec
contributions: Motivates separate short-term and long-term preference representations with adaptive fusion.
limitations: Its larger architecture and reported results do not establish the value of a minimal residual here.

related_work.title: Revisiting Graph Projections
contributions: Motivates directed interaction evidence for complementary recommendations.
limitations: Observed transitions cannot establish equipment compatibility or whether a purchase satisfied a need.

related_work.title: TensorFlow candidate sampling derivation
contributions: Explains how candidate-sampling objectives and probability corrections depend on sampling conventions.
limitations: Does not justify interpreting uncorrected 65-entry candidate cross-entropy as unbiased full-catalogue softmax.

related_work.title: SciPy bootstrap documentation
contributions: Documents paired bootstrap resampling principles applicable to fixed-model per-user comparisons.
limitations: Category stratification must be implemented explicitly; intervals do not account for adaptive model selection or training randomness.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Explains why sampled ranking metrics can disagree with full-catalogue rankings.
limitations: Does not change the required pinned benchmark; conclusions must remain specific to its candidate protocol.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains selection optimism from repeatedly using validation outcomes to choose models.
limitations: Ordinary bootstrap intervals around an adaptively selected winner do not remove this bias.

related_work.title: Hyperband
contributions: Motivates prespecified resource allocation and successive promotion of promising configurations.
limitations: Early rankings may favor faster-learning configurations; screening is not a substitute for full-length comparison.
